decision_problem: Choose the transformation path for modernizing fare payment without exclusion or service disruption.
root_non_achievedness: What are the materially distinct admissible transformation paths for City bus ticketing modernization, what unresolved distinctions separate those paths, and what missing facts block commitment?

candidate_paths.title: Path A: conservative modernization
candidate_paths.summary: Improve the closed-loop fare system first, then add compatibility and inspection tools.
required_information: whether phased validator upgrades can be funded inside the annual cap

candidate_paths.title: Path B: coordinated leap
candidate_paths.summary: Move directly to account-based contactless payment.
required_information: whether banking and legal dependencies can be satisfied before launch

dominant_distinctions.title: Phased compatibility versus direct open-loop leap
dominant_distinctions.description: The main separation is whether the city preserves a staged compatibility path or commits immediately to open-loop payment.

dominant_distinctions.title: Inclusion buffering versus maximum performance
dominant_distinctions.description: The staged path protects riders without bank cards, while the leap path maximizes performance but heightens inclusion risk.

ambiguities: The use case frames good path families more clearly than formal single-transition decisions.
missing_information: The current satisfaction status of banking and legal dependencies is not stated.
